# Nation As God-Machine

**Aliases:** nation as god, nation-state as sacred machine, national person, war body.

> **Fast answer:** Nation as god-machine names Jiang's model of the modern nation as a sacred artificial person. School, myth, welfare, production, population, and war teach individuals to imagine the nation as a body that deserves love, service, sacrifice, and death.

## What Jiang Means

The nation is a fiction that becomes real because people are trained to love it. It remembers, suffers, demands, rewards, and punishes as if it were a person. That sacred person then becomes machine-like: it organizes population, factories, soldiers, welfare, education, and death into war capacity.

This is why Jiang places the nation near religion. It creates an object of loyalty large enough to ask for the person's future, body, and children.

## How To Use This Term

Use this term when Jiang is explaining nationhood as sacred loyalty converted into population, welfare, military, and production machinery.

Do not use it for a casual reference to any country.
